nodes.name: Sagittarius A* (Galactic Center)
nodes.note: Supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, about 4.3 million solar masses. The Sun orbits it once every ~230 million years.

nodes.name: Gaia BH1
nodes.note: Closest known black hole (found 2022), ~9.6 solar masses, orbited by a Sun-like star.

nodes.name: Gaia BH3
nodes.note: Most massive stellar black hole known in the Milky Way, ~33 solar masses (2024).

nodes.name: A0620-00 (V616 Mon)
nodes.note: ~6.6 solar masses; one of the nearest X-ray binaries.

nodes.name: Gaia BH2
nodes.note: ~8.9 solar masses with a red-giant companion (2023).

nodes.name: XTE J1118+480
nodes.note: ~7 solar masses, far above the galactic plane in the halo.

nodes.name: Cygnus X-1
nodes.note: First black hole ever identified (1971), ~21 solar masses, feeding from a blue supergiant.

nodes.name: V404 Cygni
nodes.note: ~9 solar masses; famous for its 2015 X-ray outburst.

nodes.name: Hyades
nodes.note: Nearest open star cluster.

nodes.name: Pleiades (M45)
nodes.note: Open cluster of ~1,000 young stars.

nodes.name: Orion Nebula (M42)
nodes.note: Nearest massive star-forming region.

nodes.name: Crab Nebula (M1)
nodes.note: Remnant of the supernova seen in 1054 AD, with a pulsar at its heart.

nodes.name: Omega Centauri
nodes.note: Largest globular cluster in the Milky Way, ~10 million stars.

nodes.name: Hercules Cluster (M13)
nodes.note: Globular cluster of ~300,000 stars.

nodes.name: Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy
nodes.note: Satellite galaxy currently being torn apart by the Milky Way.

nodes.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
nodes.note: Satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, visible from the southern hemisphere.

nodes.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
nodes.note: Satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

nodes.name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
nodes.note: Nearest large spiral galaxy, ~1 trillion stars; will merge with the Milky Way in ~4.5 billion years.

nodes.name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
nodes.note: Third-largest galaxy in the Local Group.

nodes.name: Virgo Cluster
nodes.note: Nearest big galaxy cluster, ~1,500 galaxies around the giant elliptical M87. Its gravity shapes our Local Group's motion.

nodes.name: Fornax Cluster
nodes.note: Second-nearest rich galaxy cluster.

nodes.name: Centaurus Cluster
nodes.note: Rich cluster in the southern sky.

nodes.name: Hydra Cluster
nodes.note: Galaxy cluster in the Hydra-Centaurus supercluster.

nodes.name: Norma Cluster (Great Attractor)
nodes.note: Heart of the Great Attractor, a mass concentration pulling the Milky Way and thousands of galaxies toward it.

nodes.name: Perseus Cluster
nodes.note: One of the most massive nearby clusters, a strong X-ray source.

nodes.name: Coma Cluster
nodes.note: ~1,000 galaxies; where Fritz Zwicky first inferred dark matter in 1933.

nodes.name: Shapley Supercluster
nodes.note: Largest concentration of galaxies in the nearby universe.

nodes.name: Sloan Great Wall
nodes.note: A filament of galaxies ~1.4 billion light-years long, one of the largest known structures.

nodes.name: 3C 273 (quasar)
nodes.note: Nearest bright quasar: a supermassive black hole ~900 million solar masses swallowing gas so violently it outshines its galaxy. Distance from redshift.

sources: 2MASS Redshift Survey (Huchra+ 2012, VizieR); distance from redshift, H0=70
